subject: Follow-up: Redwood discovery + procurement questions
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 Nov 2025 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Redwood discovery + procurement questions

Hi Sofia — great to meet you and the Acme team earlier today. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery call: 

- Recap:
  - You’re looking to pilot Redwood hosted inference for a customer-facing routing assistant (expected ~50–75k tokens/day during pilot).
  - Key procurement questions: PO vs card, whether marketplace purchase is an option, and expected timeline for legal review.
  - Security checklist: SOC 2 and data residency questions flagged by your legal team.

- Immediate asks (from your side):
  1) Confirm whether you prefer to transact via PO or card (or marketplace).
  2) Share procurement contact + legal reviewer (you mentioned Carlos and Maya).
  3) Any target go-live / pilot start date?

- Our proposed next steps:
  - I’ve attached a draft SOW (SOW-Acme-Redwood-v1.pdf) and our PO terms (Redwood-PO-terms.pdf) for procurement to review.
  - Dev will follow up with a short implementation plan and resource estimate.
  - Weekly 15-min check-ins until procurement clears — propose Wednesdays 9am PT.

Attachments: SOW-Acme-Redwood-v1.pdf (63 KB), Redwood-PO-terms.pdf (18 KB)

If it helps, we can also route the commercial through AWS Marketplace for a faster procurement flow — happy to explain pros/cons. Tell me who to add to the weekly check-in invite and we’ll get started.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few quick items from procurement/legal that I wanted to surface: 

1) Does Redwood accept purchase orders for hosted API usage, or is that only available for Dedicated/Private contracts?
2) Do you have a marketplace listing (AWS or Azure) so we can buy through our AWS marketplace contract?
3) Can you share a pricing table (monthly/annual) and standard payment terms (Net 30/60)?
4) Legal would like SOC 2 Type II evidence and a brief note on data residency for logs/metrics.
5) Procurement prefers to see an SOW and the PO terms; we’ll likely share a redline.

I’m looping in Procurement (Carlos) and Legal (Maya) so they can coordinate review. Our target is to have a pilot contract in place by the end of November if possible.

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 04 Nov 2025 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood discovery + procurement questions

Hi Sofia — great to meet you all. Quick answers to procurement/legal items: 

- Payment / commercial path:
  - We accept PO for Dedicated and Private engagements. For hosted (self-serve) we typically accept card, but for customers of your size we can support a hosted PO under a commercial agreement.
  - We are listed on AWS Marketplace (Redwood Inference, LLC). Marketplace purchases can be faster because your procurement team can use existing marketplace contracts. If you’d prefer the marketplace route we can share the listing link and steps.
  - Standard payment terms: Net 30; we can consider Net 45 on a case-by-case basis for annual commitments.

- Security/compliance:
  - SOC 2 Type II report: we can share a redacted report under an NDA.
  - Data residency: logs and metrics are stored in your selected region for Dedicated/Private; hosted has regional storage options and we can log the agreed retention in the SOW.

- Documents attached: Redwood-PO-terms.pdf (standard PO language), and I’ve included a link to our compliance pack in the related links.

Proposed next steps:
1) Procurement to confirm preferred commercial path (PO vs marketplace).
2) If PO, please share your PO template and any required clauses for legal to review — we’ll return a redline.
3) Schedule a 30-min procurement call with Carlos + Maya + our legal ops if helpful.

I’ll let Dev follow up with the technical onboarding plan after we lock the commercial path.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aisha.rahman@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia@acme-logistics.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acme-logistics.com>

Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 09:00:00 -0800
Subject: Quick check-in: where is it stuck?

Hi Sofia / Carlos / Maya — following up on the SOW and PO terms I shared last week. Wanted to check where this is in your queue and whether there’s anything we can do to accelerate. 

Options we can offer to speed procurement:
- Route through AWS Marketplace (fastest for procurement teams with marketplace contracts).
- Sign our standard SOW + PO terms; we can fast-track legal review if you share a clean PO template.
- If legal needs to propose redlines, we can set up a 30-min triage with our legal ops to go clause-by-clause.

I’ve re-attached the SOW for convenience. If weekly check-ins would help, we can start them this week — propose Wed 9am PT.

Attachments: SOW-Acme-Redwood-v1.pdf

Thanks,
Marissa
From: Procurement Team <procurement@acme-logistics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sofia Martinez <sofia@acme-logistics.com>, Maya Patel <maya.patel@acme-log.com>, Carlos Reyes <carlos.reyes@acme-logistics.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 11:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick check-in: where is it stuck?

Hi Marissa — thanks for the follow-up and for the attachments. Status update from our side: 

- Legal is the blocker right now. Main items they’ve flagged: a) liability cap language; b) data residency and access to logs for customer support; c) indemnity carve-outs for third-party data.
- Procurement prefers to pay via PO (budget has to flow through our finance systems). Marketplace is an option but we need to confirm internal approvals — marketplace purchases still require PO creation on our side.
- We’ll share our PO template and a redline next week; can you confirm how quickly Redwood can return a reviewed redline?

If you can provide a short note explaining typical liability caps for customers in our industry and an appendix with data residency options we can hand to legal, that would be helpful. Also please confirm if SOC 2 can be provided under NDA.

Hi Sofia — Vivek here (Sales Lead). Thanks for the update and for looping procurement/legal in. Two quick points to help unblock: 

1) If Acme can commit to a PO by Nov 30 for the pilot (monthly billed), we can provide a one-time onboarding credit equivalent to 1 month of usage and commit a named CSM to shorten ramp time.
2) We’ll prioritize legal review if you can share your redline by EOD next Wednesday — our legal ops will return a consolidated response within 3 business days for standard commercial clauses.

For legal context, typical liability cap for customers of this profile is 1x–3x the contract value or $1M minimum; we can provide precedent language and an explanation note for your counsel. SOC 2 Type II can be shared under NDA — I’ve asked our compliance team to prepare a redacted packet.
